author: letmethink
text_post: I want to date, I really do. But I m starting to think since I ve been with no girl for so long, my mentality and behavior has made it practically impossible for me to pursue dating with women.  Every time I feel like I m coming into a situation that might lead to a dating opportunity I instinctively withdraw from the situation. An example of this was last Friday night where I meet a couple of girls who are friends with a friend of mine. The two girls are actually dating one another but as my friend explain they're in an open relationship and were open to meeting guys.  Long story short after spending a few hours playing pool with them the girls were heading out so I was saying good bye to them but the girl who I spoke with longer just stood there in front of me. I thought maybe she didn't hear me say bye so I said bye again this time a bit awkwardly, but she was still standing there staring at me. At this point I get the tightening sensation in my neck I usually get when I suspect there's an opening with a girl and my natural instinct was to just way her good bye against and meekly walk way to the pool table and act like nothing was going on.  I don't know how I m going to overcome this. I was fine with the girls that night right up that point, and that's often the case with girls, I can be ok and maybe even outgoing around them when its just being friendly, but as soon as it takes a turn towards a dating or flirting situation I just want to get out of there. I suspect it a weird defensive reaction to fearing how awkward I might be if I actually go for these situations.  The best way I can put it is, it doesn't feel like flirting with girls is something I would do, it feels so alien. It doesn't help that I have a bunch of things in my life I m not proud about, namely: -Still living at my dad's place.  -Having an old beat up car which I spend very little time maintaining  -A messy room with barely anything interesting in it,  The bit about my bedroom is particularly noteworthy because its emblematic of my lifestyle and state of mind and why I m so ill suited to dating. Basically because I ve been living my life since I can remember solely with myself in mind and since I have always been a pretty simple guy who never really needed anything fancy or interesting to be stimulated I don't have much in my bedroom and I seek interesting stuff outside with my friends. So yes this means I don't really have any hobbies. I am interested in tons of things but never to the point of actually pursing it as a hobby. I could even say I ve been living my life on autopilot since late high school, basically doing the minimum it takes to push ahead with the big things, i.e. higher education and getting a job, but everything else has been pretty much a shoulder shrugg. I need a break from all my problems to restart my life more spirited but as I get older life just keeps getting more complicated and demanding. I can't even get a breather most weeks between working full time in a lab and finishing my grad school. At the same time I m tired of waiting, I want to enjoy life while I m still young and my looks haven't faded, being  "successful" when I m middle aged would be of little consolation to me. But time passes so fast.

author: silvereagle
text_post: Other than the fact that I haven't really been anywhere near a lab, your experiences mirror my own in many ways. That is opportunities come from left field - you never see them coming - and because you have no self-esteem or much experience if any, with girls, you just freeze. And the opportunity passes, only adding to your sense of frustration and longing, and the sense that it's all just passing you by. And it is. I have to change my mindset, get out of the emotional hell I am in, not even get out of it, but just find some kind of anchor, some kind of a rope that can pull me out. And yet here I am, approaching fifty, more horny than I have ever been, and losing the plot. I try to keep perspective - I am one suffering man in a world of suffering billions, I mean the horrors that go on - but as we all know, suffering is by its nature self-consuming. Difficult to see past it. However let me stress, in closing, I cannot just meet some woman, even if it happens by accident, and then ask her out, and hope something happens from there, UNLESS I sort out my mental state first. I need some kind of mental primal-scream-shamanic-initation-breakdown-in-the-desert-psychic-trip before I even make any attempt here, because I feel as the American Indian writer Sherman Alexie put it, like a pillar of ash, and the slightest touch and I will fall apart. Watch them have sex with each other, and then fucked the both of 'em.  THE ULTIMATE MALE FANTASY. But you blew it.      If it's any comfort I have blown these kinds of opportunities, for years and decades even. Okay it's no comfort. We are all in this together. Alone. And yes you are right, before you know it you are middle-aged, and your looks are gone. And you will be haunted by these memories that risk driving you insane, and yet you will continue to pine for hot young things, who are only born about now. You think you are neurotic now? You have no idea what lies ahead. I don't say this to make you depressed, but to let you know that no matter how slim the odds, you have to change something. And you are right, the problem lies with the MIND, if you don't sort that out, it doesn't matter how much money you earn, how well you dress, you are not going to get anywhere; you will just freeze like me. I also think you keep your bedroom a mess, subconsciously, it gives you an excuse not to invite women back to your place. It's just one way of perpetuating your incel status, your seeming fear of intimacy. I mean if your bedroom is neat and presentable and you could actually fuck a woman there, then you can't cook up some excuse to yourself, not to invite a woman back there so easily. I myself stay in a tiny apartment, but at least it's just me there. I can't invite a woman back there because it's also a mess, and my downstairs area doesn't even have any furniture, it's really very bare. I can't invite anybody back in fact, even a friend. I keep putting off buying some furniture (I can afford getting a few things, some chairs, a table, a few paintings second hand), it also gives me the excuse not to bring a woman back if the opportunity even came up. So now I am fantasizing, obsessing about that neighbor of mine I mention above, the cute, blonde 23 year old (25 years younger than me), who I reckon sleeps naked in the sweltering summer heat on her bed which is a mere three to six feet from mine, (and I sleep naked too in summer) we share a dividing wall and both our bedrooms are upstairs, our beds on either side of the wall, our mattresses almost right up against the shared wall. It's how I know when she fucks and even masturbates. It turns me on and yet it's driving me crazy. I sometimes don't sleep for hours thinking about her lying SO NEAR ME, naked, her pussy, her breasts just there, so near yet so far. Never mind my numerous neuroses, what chance do I stand with a young woman whose parents are probably my age? This is your future if you don't do something to change. It gets worse over time, as you fear and intuit. Way worse. You don't want to end up like me. The remorse, the longing for a past that never was. And you will pine for these girls you are messing it up with even more in twenty years time than now. And yes the same girls.  So we have to do something about our mental/emotional makeup. The mind is everything. It is psychological trauma that got us here in the first place after all. I am sure this must be the case with you too, because you are clearly not unattractive, otherwise why are these girls interested in you? And as you have heard from your parents, uncles, grandparents and anybody over 40, the years go by faster and faster and faster the older you get. In fact this all becomes another neurosis, because it's a case of - what do you mean the year 2000 was 18 years ago, it was five years ago max. And not as a joke neither. You think some Time God stole all the years from you, as if you were in a coma and then woke up.  You think you are experiencing sexual frustration now, a remorseless unsatisfied longing, regret, self-loathing? You have no idea what lies ahead. It becomes cumulative. Not just more of the same. It intensifies in these terrible feedback loops. One's sanity is severely threatened.  What we need is courage. I don't know where it is going to come from, because well I just don't know. But I am increasingly recognizing what I lack is courage, more than anything. It seems obvious now but I don't think I really saw it for decades. Only courage can maybe cut through the Gordian Knot of our incel nightmares.

author: TransCel
text_post: I'm so mentalcel right now I can't even go out on dates, but that's actually due partially to physical health issues. In Mark Manson's book, Models: Attract Women With Honesty, he says that living with your parents can affect how well you do with women. In his audio book, he said that even happened to him when he moved back in with his parents (or I think maybe he was just visiting them) Quote:Men often don’t totally believe me, but poor lifestyle choices afflict all of your interactions and communication when it comes to women. Poor lifestyle choices reflect a lack of investment in yourself, which in turn causes you to be less confident around others for validation. I first noticed this when I worked with men who still lived at home with their parents. A lot of these men were great guys. They were smart, funny, caring, had interesting hobbies. Some even had a good job, but they stayed with their parents for other reasons (health, etc.) Yet they got absolutely no results. Women never responded warmly to them, and they never seemed quite as motivated or as confident. There’s a certain baseline level of independence and self-sufficiency that your lifestyle must give you for you to be able to move forward. If you’re constantly stressed by work, upset by your friends, and in poor health, then no amount of work on your anxieties and communication is going to help much. You’re effectively putting a ceiling on your development and your potential with women. The other two parts of this book will not be much use to you. You can try, but I can tell you, you probably won’t see much change in your results. Get your life taken care of. Get healthy. Find a happy group of friends. Find a few hobbies that you love. Develop opinions. Start caring about what you spend your time doing. This increases your self-investment and will make you less needy around others.  This, in turn, will give you the courage to take the correct action and the wherewithal to communicate effectively. This is honest living. And once you’re living a life true to yourself, your values and your ideals, then it’s time to take action.
